name-omits-visible-label-text: A control's spoken name leaves out the words printed on it, so a voice-control user who says the visible label can't activate the control.
name-present-but-not-descriptive-of-purp: A button has a screen-reader name like 'button' or an icon filename, so the user hears something but still has no idea what the control does.
wrong-role-valid-but-inappropriate: A toggle switch is coded as a checkbox (or a heading, link, etc.), so the screen reader announces the wrong kind of control and the user misjudges how to use it.
stale-or-contradicting-state-value: A toggle looks ON but is still coded as 'off' (aria-checked false), so the screen reader tells the user the opposite of what's actually showing on screen.
stale-text-alternative-on-dynamic-named-: A button's content changes by script, but its screen-reader name stays frozen on the old content, so the user is told about something that's no longer there.
value-not-settable-or-change-not-notifie: A custom slider or switch only updates its value for mouse users, so a keyboard or screen-reader user can't change it or never hears that it changed.
iframe-name-does-not-describe-content: An embedded frame has a vague title like 'iframe' or 'content', so a screen-reader user jumping between frames can't tell what each one actually contains.
multipart-field-subnames-ambiguous: A phone or date split into several inputs labels every box the same ('Phone', 'Phone', 'Phone'), so a screen-reader user can't tell which box is which part.
